sources: WEDNESDAY Oct 28 2026 RUN, pre-US-open (before 13:30 UTC), FOMC DECISION DAY (statement 2pm EDT / 18:00 UTC, target 3.75-4.00 pct). This run has TUESDAY'S FULL US CLOSES plus FRED prints through Oct 26-27, so only the plumbing and MOVE tiles are carries. HEADLINE: THE OIL PREMIUM REFUSES TO DIE AND THE CURVE KEEPS FLATTENING INTO THE FED. EQUITIES - SECOND STRAIGHT RISK-ON SESSION. Tuesday Oct 27 closed green across the board: S&P 500 7,722.60 plus 0.60 pct (plus 45.83 pts, range 7,677.16-7,736.24), Nasdaq Composite 26,477.81 plus 1.18 pct (plus 308.43 pts) on a chip-led AI rally, Dow 52,377.57 plus 0.03 pct. VOL - EQUITY VOL BREAKS TO A NEW MONTH LOW. VIX 17.53 for the Oct 27 close, minus 4.7 pct from 18.39 (FRED VIXCLS has now posted Oct 26 at 18.39, revising up the 18.27 third-party print carried last run; Oct 27 not yet on FRED, Yahoo intraday showed 17.57-17.59). That is the LOWEST VIX of October and the second large daily drop in three sessions. Versus 17.31 on Oct 21 it is plus 1.3 pct, so the tile trend stays FLAT even though the level is at the bottom of the range. MOVE is CARRIED at 103.31 for Oct 23 for a THIRTEENTH consecutive blind run - Investing.com still serves Oct 23 as its last row (106.84 Oct 22, 95.94 Oct 21, 101.70 Oct 20, 101.30 Oct 19, 101.10 Oct 16), CNBC returned a client error and MacroMicro failed to load again. Against the Oct 21 print of 95.94 the carry would read plus 7.7 pct, but Oct 21 was an outlier low inside the Oct 22-23 vol spike; against Oct 16 (101.10) it is plus 2.2 pct, so the tile is held FLAT and should be treated as stale, not as a measurement. OIL - THE FADE REVERSES, RAS TANURA CLAIMED. Brent 115.92 USD (TradingEconomics stats, plus 1.79 pct; live widget 116.057 plus 1.91 pct and ticker 116.06-116.071, dispersion about 15bp, does not change the read), after a 113.72-113.88 Tuesday close that was minus 1.67 to minus 1.8 pct on the day. WTI about 101.1-101.4 (plus 1.15 to 1.47 pct) after 99.83-99.90 Tuesday. So the Monday-Tuesday fade has been FULLY RETRACED and Brent is back above the Friday settle. THE DRIVER IS NEW: on Tuesday Oct 27 the Houthis claimed a BALLISTIC MISSILE STRIKE ON RAS TANURA, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, 550,000 b/d per Reuters. Saudi authorities did NOT confirm the strike and there is NO information on damage or disruption. So the TENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN closes with the same qualifier: still not one hit on Saudi oil infrastructure independently confirmed. The claim has escalated from shipping and interceptions to a named strategic refinery, but until Riyadh confirms damage this remains headline premium, not a lost barrel. Versus 110.40 on Oct 21 Brent is plus 5.0 pct, trend clearly UP. Supply context: US crude inventories seen plus about 15,000 bbl for the week ended Oct 23 (Reuters poll of eight analysts); OPEC+ expected to HOLD December targets at Sunday's meeting. METALS - GOLD BACK OVER 4,000, COPPER AT A NEW HIGH. Gold 4,030.55 USD/t.oz minus 0.73 pct this morning (headline 4,031.60 minus 0.70 pct, table 4,031.48 minus 0.71 pct) after a strong Tuesday (HDFC 4,075 plus 0.9 pct). Copper 6.6245 USD/Lbs minus 0.04 pct (stats 6.62 minus 0.08 pct), up from 6.53 last run. Copper-gold 6.6245/4030.55*1000 = 1.6436, tile 1.63 to 1.64, up from 1.59 on Oct 21. Trend UP, third consecutive run of improvement, and still the cleanest pro-growth signal on the board. DOLLAR - THE ANOMALY FINALLY CRACKS, A LITTLE. DXY 102.43 plus 0.11 pct (stats 102.4296 plus 0.04 pct, markets table 102.412 plus 0.09 pct), after about 102.32-102.33 plus 0.35-0.4 pct on Tuesday. Versus 101.79 on Oct 21 that is plus 0.63 pct, the first week-on-week move big enough to flip the tile from flat to UP after TEN runs of a flat dollar. Still a modest move and it is happening INTO the Fed, not out of a risk event. Tile 102.10 to 102.43, trend up. CURVE - FLATTEST OF THE MONTH, NOW THROUGH TUESDAY. FRED T10Y2Y Oct 27 at 0.29 (0.32 Oct 26, 0.31 Oct 23, 0.31 Oct 22, 0.32 Oct 21). That is a NEW OCTOBER LOW and down 9bp from the 0.38 of a week ago. Trend DOWN. Tuesday's intraday tape around the meeting start: 2Y 4.73 pct, 5Y 4.839 pct, 10Y 4.99 pct, 30Y 5.31 pct - the 10Y is back below 5.00 pct while the 2Y keeps grinding up, which is exactly how you get 0.29. BREAKEVEN - THE BREAK HOLDS, FIFTH SESSION. FRED T5YIFR Oct 26 at 2.21 pct (2.20 Oct 23, 2.19 Oct 22, 2.34 Oct 21, 2.31 Oct 20). Up 1bp on the day but still 10bp BELOW the 2.31 of a week ago, and this is WITH Brent back near 116 and a named Saudi refinery under claimed attack. The market is still flatly refusing to price the oil shock as an inflation shock. Trend DOWN. This remains the single most important fact going into the 2pm statement. CREDIT - THE FRIDAY WIDE IS BEING REPAIRED. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 HAS NOW POSTED Oct 26 at 3.30 pct, 8bp TIGHTER than Oct 23's 3.38 and 10bp inside the Oct 22 month wide of 3.40 (3.27 Oct 21, 3.33 Oct 20). Tile 338 to 330bp. Versus 329bp on Oct 21 that is plus 1bp, i.e. FLAT on the week - the trend flips down from up as the one-day credit event fully unwinds. Oct 27 not yet posted. MACRO TILES - ALL CARRIED, NO NEW RELEASES SINCE THE LAST RUN. LEI y/y plus 1.2 pct September (index 99.6) versus minus 0.7 pct on Oct 21, trend up, still the biggest week-on-week improvement on the board. Consumer sentiment 48.0 UMich October final versus 46.3 a week ago, trend up, but 48.0 is still a five-month low in level terms. Jobless claims 194k week ending Oct 17 (three-month low) versus 199k, trend down; continuing claims about 1.73 million, a six-week high - little firing, visibly less hiring; NEXT RELEASE TOMORROW Thursday Oct 29. ISM Manufacturing 54.5 September, next Nov 2. Sahm Rule 0.00 September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50. Building permits 1,400k SAAR September, next mid-November. NFCI minus 0.496 week ending Oct 16 (minus 0.502 Oct 9, minus 0.508 Oct 2, minus 0.518 Sep 25, minus 0.528 Sep 18) - the Oct 23 read is due TODAY Oct 28 at 8:30 ET, AFTER this run, and will be the first NFCI containing both the Oct 22 and Oct 23 risk-off sessions. Carried for one more run. Global liquidity 1 (stable) on the Oct 21 Fed H.4.1, total assets 6,753,604 million USD, minus 2,035 million on the week, plus 2.5 pct on the year; no regime change at the ECB, PBOC or BOJ; next H.4.1 Thursday Oct 29. MONETARY PLUMBING - BLIND, THIRTEENTH RUN. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION at 0bp, NOT a measurement; every free source serves a SOFR level or an OIS rate but never the spread. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is likewise a STANDING ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp. Two assumed tiles plus one judgement tile (global liquidity) plus one stale tile (MOVE) out of eighteen - the worst data-quality count of the month, unchanged for a thirteenth run. CALENDAR: FOMC statement TODAY Oct 28 2pm EDT, target 3.75-4.00 pct, CME-implied probability of a HIKE about 10 pct i.e. a HOLD is the overwhelming base case, with scope for a hike still priced before year-end. NFCI today 8:30 ET. September PCE Thursday Oct 29. Jobless claims Thursday Oct 29. H.4.1 Thursday Oct 29. OPEC+ Sunday Nov 1. ISM Nov 2. Midterms Nov 3. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy before this run (HEAD a7899d9, Oct 27 commit), this scheduled session remains the SOLE writer of data.json, the GitHub Action stays disabled since Oct 17, BDTI stays removed since Oct 17. The .git lock-file pile keeps growing (HEAD.lock, HEAD.lock.*.bak, index.lock.stale.* and similar, about 165 at the last count plus this run's) because this session cannot delete files in the folder; harmless so far but it WILL eventually break a git operation and clearing it needs delete permission on the Dashboard Macro folder. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, THIRTEENTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in PLAIN TEXT in .git/config; it is fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Untracked junk still in the repo root: _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: the Oct 22-23 risk scare is now almost fully walked back on the financial tiles - equity vol at a month low, HY 10bp inside the month wide, two green equity sessions - while the oil premium has REBUILT on a named refinery claim that nobody has confirmed. The growth tiles are the best they have been all month (LEI y/y positive, claims at a three-month low, sentiment up, copper-gold at a new high). What has NOT repaired is the price of money: the curve is at a new October low of 0.29 and the 5y5y breakeven is 10bp lower than a week ago with Brent near 116. So the board going into the 2pm statement reads GROWTH-OK, INFLATION-FADING, CURVE-FLATTENING, with the dovish tail live and nothing in the hard data broken. The one genuinely new risk is binary and headline-driven: a CONFIRMED hit on Ras Tanura would take this from a premium story to a barrel story. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: the FOMC statement today and whether it treats the oil shock as transitory (the breakeven says the market already has); whether Riyadh confirms ANY damage at Ras Tanura; the Oct 28 NFCI, first read with both risk-off sessions; September PCE tomorrow; whether T10Y2Y breaks below 0.29; whether HY keeps grinding tighter when Oct 27 posts; OPEC+ Sunday; rotating the embedded PAT; clearing the .git lock files.
